brief: A warm humanist sans for interfaces and text: friendly and clear, not corporate, with some calligraphic life. Must work at 13-16 px and in paragraphs.

why.x_height: 520/1000 is generous, so letters stay open and legible at interface sizes.
why.stem: 90 is a regular weight that holds up on screen; raised from 86 after the drawing test looked light.
why.thin: 72 (a 0.8 ratio) is low contrast, enough to feel drawn but not to thin out at 13 px.
why.stress_deg: -10 tilts the axis like a broad-nib pen, which supplies the calligraphic warmth.
why.join: Arches thin to half width at stems, which keeps n, m and r counters open at small sizes.
why.proportions: Round capitals are wide and E, F, L, S and B narrow, following classical humanist proportions.
why.apertures: Open terminals on a, c, e and s stop those letters closing up at small sizes.
why.kern_gap: 95 sits between round-round (84) and stem-stem (152) spacing, so open pairs like A V and T o close up without crowding.
why.l_tail: The lowercase l has a small tail so l, I and 1 stay distinct in interface text.
why.optical_spacing: Letters space from measured white space. A depth of 70 and factor of 0.9 land near this font's earlier by-eye values, so S (76) is the one spacing dial for letters.
